title: EvalPort ResultSet
description: The output of running an eval suite — results and summary statistics.

version.description: EvalPort specification version. Full semver 2.0.0 (https://semver.org): MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional -PRERELEASE and +BUILD metadata, e.g. "1.0.0", "1.0.0-draft", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.1.0-beta.2+build.5".

suite_id.description: ID of the eval suite that was run.

suite_version.description: Version of the eval suite that was run.

provider.description: Provider configuration used for the run.

isolation.description: Trial isolation mode for repeated attempts represented in this ResultSet's results (see attempt, below): whether repeats ran in fresh sessions/model instances or a shared session/context, which changes what a stability or flip-rate computation over those repeats can actually support statistically. An open string, not a closed enum -- "fresh" and "shared" are conventional values, not an exhaustive list, so a new isolation strategy never needs a spec change just to be nameable. Declared once per ResultSet, not per Result: a single ResultSet is one collection of evidence and should make one isolation claim; a producer whose repeats genuinely mix isolation modes SHOULD emit separate ResultSets rather than mix modes within one (see Extension Mechanism -> Repetition & Attempt Tracking). Absent means unknown/not declared -- existing ResultSets need no change.

group.description: Membership of this ResultSet in a named group of sibling ResultSets -- a sweep, a mutation-testing run, a multi-model comparison, or similar. The join key lives here on the member (mirroring W&B Sweep.sweep_id and MLflow's parent-run link), not on a separate group document: EvalPort has no place to durably store a 'group object' independent of its members, and precedent from W&B/MLflow/Stryker's mutation-testing-report-schema is that the rollup itself is consumer-computed, not schema-mandated. Absent means this ResultSet is not part of a declared group -- existing ResultSets need no change. See Extension Mechanism -> Grouped/Sibling ResultSets and Discussion #45 (landed in PR #54, 2026-09-20).

group_id.description: Identifier shared by every ResultSet in this group. An open string with producer-chosen scheme (UUID, slug, timestamp-based, ...), the same design as suite_id/run_id -- EvalPort does not mint or validate identifiers, it just requires them to be stable and unique enough for a consumer to group on.

parent_group_id.description: Optional identifier of a PARENT group this group is itself nested under, letting groups form a chain (grandparent group -> parent group -> this group) the same way a single MLflow run's parent_run_id can itself point to a run that has its own parent_run_id, producing an arbitrarily deep tree from nothing but one pointer per node (verified against mlflow/tracking/fluent.py's active_run_stack, and against real 3-level GrandParent/Parent/Child usage in mlflow/mlflow#16685) -- not every grouping system has this: W&B's Run.sweep_id and its separate wandb.init(group=...) primitive are both flat, single-level, with no parent construct in wandb/wandb's source. This field lets EvalPort represent either shape: omit it for a flat group (the only shape this field supported before this addition -- every existing group-bearing ResultSet needs no change), or set it to model a sweep-of-sweeps, a hierarchical mutation-testing campaign (e.g. one parent group per source file, child groups per mutant within that file), or any other producer-defined nesting. MUST NOT equal this object's own group_id (a group cannot be its own parent). EvalPort does not itself resolve or validate the chain across documents -- like group_id, this is a join key a consumer follows across the full set of ResultSets it has, not something a single document's own validity can fully confirm (a dangling or cyclic parent_group_id across documents is a producer bug, not something one document's schema validation can see). See Extension Mechanism -> Grouped/Sibling ResultSets.

role.description: Open string naming this member's role or outcome within the group, e.g. "mutant", "seed", "baseline", "candidate". Not a closed enum, for the same reason ResultSet.isolation isn't one: a new grouping strategy should never need a spec change just to be nameable. Absent means unspecified role.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for this member, e.g. "mutant_017 (relational-operator-swap in billing.py:42)" or "seed=1337". For display; not a join key.

sequence.description: Optional 0-indexed position of this ResultSet within its group, for producers that know the group's total size at emission time (e.g. mutant 17 of 240). Absent means unknown or not applicable -- consumers MUST NOT assume contiguous or complete sequences from a partial set of group members.

results.description: One result per test case, or -- when using attempt -- multiple results per test case representing repeated trials of it.

test_case_id.description: ID of the test case this result corresponds to.

actual_output.description: The output produced by the LLM.

attempt.description: 1-indexed repetition number for this test_case_id within this run_id; ascending values are observation order (attempt 2 was observed after attempt 1, etc.), giving consumers a documented ordering guarantee instead of having to infer one from completed_at or array position. Absent, or 1 with no sibling attempts, means a single-attempt result -- existing single-shot ResultSets need no change. Together with test_case_id and run_id this forms the join key for pairing repeated trials of the same case (e.g. LangSmith's num_repetitions, Promptfoo's per-test repeats, Inspect AI's epochs) for stability/flip-rate analysis; (test_case_id, run_id, attempt) MUST be unique across results when attempt is present -- see Validation Rules -> Uniqueness and Extension Mechanism -> Repetition & Attempt Tracking.

completed_at.description: Timestamp this individual result was produced (ISO 8601). Optional; distinct from the ResultSet-level completed_at, which marks when the whole run finished. Lets a resumed or incrementally-written run establish a per-result tiebreaker when merging two partial ResultSets for the same run_id -- see Extension Mechanism -> Resumable Runs & Partial ResultSets.

score.description: Numeric score, typically 0.0-1.0. Null if skipped or errored.

error.description: Error details if the test case errored.
